lesson.grammar_point: -ed and -ing adjectives (excited / exciting, tired / tiring: -ed for the feeling, -ing for the thing that causes it)

listenings.text: Hi Renato, it's Dana. First, congratulations again. I was so excited on Sunday, and I'm still thrilled today. That last wave was amazing. Now, about this week. I know you're exhausted. The trip was long and tiring, so tomorrow there's no training. Just rest, go to bed early, and do some easy stretches. On Wednesday we're back in the water. On Thursday, after training, we're going to watch the replay of your heat together. It isn't boring, I promise. We can learn a lot from it. And one more thing. Everybody is going to give you a lot of attention this week. That's nice, but stay focused. The semifinal date isn't confirmed yet. The organizers might announce it this week. Okay? See you on Wednesday.

Hey everyone, it's Kai, the squad captain. A lot of you asked for this, so here's the replay of Renato's last wave in the quarterfinal. Watch the start. There's one minute left, and he's in third place. Very stressful! Then the set comes, and he doesn't hesitate. First turn, good. Second turn, better. And the third turn is the surprising one. Look at the spray! The crowd on the beach was amazed, and honestly, so was I. Some people think surf contests are boring to watch. They're not! This was the most exciting heat of the day. Okay, that's it. Like the video, and come and watch the semifinal later this month.

items.situation: A girl in your class says: "I saw your wave on the club page!" Answer her, and don't show off.
Bev asks: "How was the drive home on Sunday?" Tell her about the trip, and how you felt.
Tom says: "Surf contests are boring." Disagree with him.
Your teacher asks: "How do you feel about the semifinal?" Give two feelings.
Your teacher asks about your life right now. Say one thing that is exciting and one thing that is boring.
